subject: Next steps & procurement frame: production inference pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Tom Evans <tevans@acmeedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & procurement frame: production inference pilot

Tom — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so your team can share internally.

Key pain points you called out
- Highly variable inference load (10x peaks) driving unacceptable tail latency during peak windows
- Current stack (SageMaker + homegrown queueing) has inconsistent p95 and poor cost visibility
- Data residency concerns for certain EU customer segments and auditability needs for API access

Goals / success criteria you mentioned
- Target p95 < 120ms for chat flows at pilot scale (~50 concurrent sessions)
- Cost estimate for steady-state and for peak handling; clear guardrails on spend for pilot
- SOC2 evidence and VPC/networking options for private data paths

What we propose as next steps (procurement-framing included)
1) Technical deep-dive with your ML infra + security (60 min) — propose Tue 8/24 or Wed 8/25. We'll bring a short benchmark plan we can run on a small token set.
2) Share SOC2 + architecture overview and a short one-pager (attached) for your security review.
3) Initial commercial guardrails: pilot PO or card for pilot cap (we find customers prefer a 30–90 day pilot with a spend cap), then reserved capacity estimate if you move to production. We'll outline two options: pay-as-you-go pilot vs. 3-month reserved pilot.
4) Please confirm procurement and legal contact so we can prep an SOW and an NDA if needed.

Attachments: redwood-onepager.pdf (intro + pilot approach), initial-sow-template.docx (template we can tailor)

If you confirm the tech dive attendee list and procurement contact, we'll get calendar invites and a short benchmark plan over.

Thanks — looking forward.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer

From: Tom Evans <tevans@acmeedge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & procurement frame: production inference pilot

Karthik — really helpful recap, thanks. A couple quick clarifications and some procurement context: 

Clarifications
- The 120ms p95 target is for our conversational frontend (100–300 token responses). We also want to capture burst behavior for longer LLM runs (up to 1k tokens) — can you include those in the benchmark plan?
- Data residency: EU subset is critical for two enterprise customers; we need an option that avoids cross-border logging for those flows.

Procurement & timeline
- Procurement contact: Lisa Park (lisa.park@acmeedge.com) — I'll loop her in below.
- Timeline: procurement prefers a 6–8 week window to evaluate pilots and sign a PO if the pilot meets objectives. For initial budget approval they want an indicative price range for a 3-month pilot (rough ballpark is fine for now).

Attendees for tech deep-dive:
- Myself (CTO sponsor)
- Rajesh Menon (Head of ML Ops) — will join for infra details
- Lisa Park (procurement) — for contract/PO questions

We can do Tuesday 8/24 at 10:00am PT. If you can send a short benchmark plan and indicative pilot pricing ahead of the call that'd be ideal.

Thanks — looping Lisa: Lisa, Karthik from Redwood. We're evaluating a production inference option to replace our current SageMaker endpoints for critical customer flows. Karthik, Lisa is procurement lead and will advise on PO/contract path.

Best,
Tom
--
Tom Evans
CTO, AcmeEdge
tevans@acmeedge.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Tom Evans <tevans@acmeedge.com>, Lisa Park <lisa.park@acmeedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & procurement frame: production inference pilot

Tom / Lisa — great, thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping Lisa in. Confirming the proposed plan and providing the initial commercial guardrails you requested.

Benchmarks & scope
- We'll include both short-chat (100–300 tokens) and long-run (up to 1k tokens) sample runs in the plan. Benchmark will capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per token at steady and burst loads.
- For EU-residency flows we can propose a private VPC option or region-pin for logs; will include explicit config notes in the security doc.

Initial commercial guardrails (indicative)
- Pilot option A (pay-as-you-go): no commitment, usage invoiced monthly. Expect a blended cost estimate of ~$1,500–$3,000/month for a 3-month small-scale pilot (final depends on token volumes in benchmark).
- Pilot option B (reserved 3-month pilot): discounted reserved capacity to cover baseline throughput; indicative committed spend $12k–$20k for 3 months (gives priority routing and lower per-token execution).
- Production/Reserved estimate modeling: we'll produce cost per 1M tokens and expected latency improvements for both options so procurement can compare.

Next steps
1) Karthik to send short benchmark plan + SOW template (attached) — done (see attachments).
2) Tech deep-dive Tue 8/24 10:00am PT — invite to follow.
3) Lisa / procurement to confirm any legal or data residency docs they need for advance review.

If this framing looks right, we'll prepare a one-pager for Lisa that highlights pilot terms and what a PO would cover (timeframe, spend cap, acceptance criteria).

Thanks — I'll follow up with calendar invites and the benchmark deck.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: prep for AcmeEdge pilot pricing and SOW

Marissa / Ben — quick internal note after looping Lisa in.

Action items I need from you before Tuesday's tech deep-dive:
- Marissa: can you draft a one-page pilot commercial summary with the two guardrails (PAYG estimate + reserved pilot range) and an acceptance criteria section we can hand to procurement? Include a note on billing cadence and pilot spend cap language.
- Ben: please prepare a short appendix on our reserved capacity sizing assumptions (GPU hours, concurrency targets) and a recommended monitoring/tracing add-on for the pilot.

Attachments to include when we send to Lisa: redwood-onepager.pdf, initial-sow-template.docx, short-benchmark-plan.md (I'll draft and send before the call).

Keep it lean — procurement likes crisp numbers and explicit PO language. I'll loop you into the tech dive invite once it's scheduled.

Thanks,
Karthik
